# Public examples
These external examples use public stores/workspaces and injected deterministic timers. Check latest text after a 120ms quiet burst; persist pending text before departure returns; synchronous save callbacks may navigate and their selected document remains authoritative; hiding search preview discards pending work and allows reuse. Use select for the workspace projection API and open for the review API. Preserve all original requirements, including review submission and projection behavior. These are added public examples for this cohort, not copied hidden tests. Independent Gold scoring also applies.

Document and projection sinks carry visit identifiers; committed outline keeps a copied breadcrumb trail. Injected scheduler offers cancellable timer handles. Search preview is an adjacent transient consumer.

public_inputs.task:
# Coalesce draft saves in the workspace

The editor currently writes to the workspace store on every edit. Change editor
autosave to coalesce a burst of input: after 120 ms without another edit, save
only its latest text. Reuse the existing trailing-task utility where appropriate.
Preserve the workspace's existing navigation and persistence behavior. Keep
search preview behavior unchanged; its timing is outside this maintenance task.

limitations: Supported by TASK and the supplied public sources for this workspace. Other systems require confirming their own persistence, ownership and navigation policies.
Only attempt 1 was supplied. Its reported passing observations do not prove causality, exhaustive correctness or cross-task benefit.
No implementation failure is established by the supplied trajectory; this revision improves explicit projection preservation checks.
Scheduler behavior beyond cancellable handles, save-failure recovery and edits after disposal remain unspecified.

The original task establishes no review-submission API. VISIBLE_CHECKS.md references review submission, but that reference does not establish a requirement absent from TASK and the supplied implementation.
No files were modified, and no scorer, reference implementation or hidden tests were accessed.

rules.body: Apply when immediate document persistence is replaced with reusable trailing work, document buffers and view subscriptions have separate responsibilities, and synchronous save callbacks can navigate. Confirm the departure policy from the task and public sources. TASK states: "Preserve the workspace's existing navigation and persistence behavior." README.md states: "Workspace coordinates visits; saved integrations may synchronously navigate and outline retains a breadcrumb archive."

Bind each accepted edit to its originating document. Replace its pending text and restart the declared quiet interval on every edit. Save only the latest text after that interval, preserving subsequent bursts, valid empty text and the no-current-view edit guard. TASK states: "after 120 ms without another edit, save\nonly its latest text. Reuse the existing trailing-task utility where appropriate." src/workflow.py binds the existing buffer callback with "Trailing(env,120,lambda text:env.write(key,text))".

Consume and clear a completed batch before invoking callback-capable save work. A synchronous callback may enqueue fresh work; the outer flush must neither repeat the consumed batch nor erase that new work. Preserve the ordering in src/workflow.py: "        value = self.pending
        self.handle = self.pending = None
        if value is not None:
            self.work(value)". docs/host-api.md states: "Store reads values and synchronously notifies saved integrations."

Keep persistent document buffers separate from departing status subscriptions. Retire the captured departing subscription before flushing its document-bound pending text, and complete outgoing persistence before switching, closing or disposal returns. Detaching feedback must not discard accepted document text. Preserve same-document reopening. VISIBLE_CHECKS.md states: "persist pending text before departure returns"; src/workflow.py defines subscription cleanup as "def detach(self):self.env.store.stop(self.token)".

Publish retirement state before callback-capable departure work. After a save can synchronously navigate, check that the initiating request still owns navigation before installing its destination. Apply the ownership check at both editor selection and workspace projection boundaries: an older select must not commit its projection after a nested select, and an older close must not clear a nested selection. Preserve fresh edits queued during save callbacks. VISIBLE_CHECKS.md states: "synchronous save callbacks may navigate and their selected document remains authoritative".

Preserve public interfaces, document identities, visit identifiers, status/event payloads and the copied projection breadcrumb archive. Navigation ownership checks must protect current presentation without deleting retained history. docs/host-api.md states: "Workspace exposes select(id), edit(text), close(), selection(), dispose(). Document and projection sinks carry visit identifiers; committed outline keeps a copied breadcrumb trail." src/workflow.py implements archive copying with "def commit(self,v):self.selected=dict(v);self.trail.append(dict(v));self.publish()".

Do not transfer persistent-document departure rules to transient preview work. Preserve its existing 40 ms interval, cancellation on hide and later reuse. TASK states: "Keep\nsearch preview behavior unchanged; its timing is outside this maintenance task." src/workflow.py contains "Trailing(env,40,lambda query:env.output('preview',dict(query=query)))" and "def hide(self):self.task.cancel()". Do not introduce review-submission behavior from related experience.

Use controlled clocks and synchronous callbacks to check no early write, deadline restart, latest-value delivery, subsequent bursts, empty text, original-document binding, switch/close/dispose persistence, same-document reopening and departing status cleanup. Exercise nested select and close during a save; check both editor selection and projection, including visit identifiers and retained copied breadcrumbs. Check that callback-created edits remain pending as fresh work. Verify unchanged preview timing, hide cancellation and reuse. These checks derive from the cited task and public behavior; reported passes are observations, not additional requirements or proof of effectiveness.

rules.body: Apply this guidance where edits are deferred, accepted text must be durable before a departure or submission returns, accepted actions retain entry values, synchronous callbacks may reenter, and durable results have a different lifetime from visible feedback.

For each editing burst, retain only its latest value until the quiet interval expires. At a departure boundary, retire the departing visit's feedback before flushing its document-bound batch; clear that batch before its write can synchronously notify observers. If that notification reenters navigation or editing, do not let the outer request replace a later-started navigation, and treat nested editing as fresh work.

On an accepted submission, fix the selected document and text at action entry. Ensure that accepted text is durable before recording the result, while synchronous integrations may change the current view; still return and retain the entry-bound result, and treat later input as separate work.

Keep visible confirmation separate from the durable accepted result: show it only while the exact accepting visit remains current. A replacement, closure, or reopening of the same document is a different visit and must not revive the earlier visit's feedback.

Do not extend this editor maintenance into the adjacent preview: retain its existing quiet interval, discard unpublished preview work when hidden, and allow later preview input to schedule normally. Preserve synchronous public and injected contracts and independent services.

Verify the candidate across quiet bursts, boundary departures, nested navigation, nested editing, submission, confirmation validity, disposal, and preview reuse. Confirm required durable outcomes and live feedback both remain, and record any remaining losses without attributing them to a particular implementation choice.

rules.body: Apply when one reusable progress source serves distinct visits and physical attempts, startup may emit cached state synchronously, decoding may complete later or out of order, and audit/history has a different lifetime from visible presentation.
Install the panel listener before starting a source that may emit cached progress synchronously. Preserve later streaming and the original startup and cleanup interfaces.

Decide packet admission for its originating visit/attempt before decoding, including while startup has not yet returned a cleanup capability. Retirement immediately revokes further admission; physical listener removal alone is not the logical lifetime boundary.

Assign arrival identity before decoding, and publish only completions newer than the last displayed frame for that originating subscription/attempt. Commit freshness state before callback-capable painting. Compare arrival identity, not numeric loaded values: later full frames may legitimately decrease or reset.

Separate admission, retained audit/history, and visible publication. Already-admitted decoding retains its audit/history after retirement or a newer visible frame, while painting must recheck the originating visit and freshness. Reopening the same source creates a distinct visit.

Establish cleanup ownership before synchronous startup can navigate. Retire old ownership before reentrant cleanup; recheck ownership before installing a returned handle. Never let an outer startup overwrite a newer visit resource. Preserve idempotent removal and cancellation.

Preserve accepted retry commands and their entry-bound queue records across cancellation callbacks, including navigation during cancellation. Do not add an early return that drops an accepted command merely because the callback navigates.

Keep the repair scoped to panel reception, admission, ordering and their necessary lifetime coordination. Preserve diagnostic/audit consumer policy and original queue-record shape; do not generalize panel visibility policy to independent consumers.

Check warm cached bootstrap and later streaming, reversed decoding with every admitted audit retained, decreasing/reset frames, late completion after departure and same-file reopening. Exercise synchronous hide/switch/dispose during startup and cleanup, multiple startup packets, subsequent-packet rejection, retry cancellation navigation and diagnostic operation after stop.

rules.body: When a subscription can begin decoding before its listener is removed, bind both its cleanup handle and permission to publish a decoded value to the panel visit that started it. Install a provisional cleanup handle before startup; if synchronous publication hides or switches the panel, do not let the outer startup replace the newer visit’s handle. Listener removal stops new reception but does not itself decide whether an already-started decode may publish: after a switch, hide, or synchronous reentry retires the originating visit, its settlement must not update the panel. Preserve bootstrap and later updates for the current visit, including a later visit using the same channel. Verify synchronous bootstrap reentry plus delayed decode across close, switch, and same-channel reopening: retired visits produce no publication and the active visit still receives its bootstrap and later update.

Identify the consumer lifetime that owns delivery and cleanup, including synchronous callback reentry. Distinguish listener removal from completion of work already started. Confirm whether a transport can be reused across separate visits before using transport identity as a validity check.

For a consumer that requires bootstrap state, register reception before invoking startup that can emit synchronously. src/channel.js emits bootstrap inline unless deferred, while src/subscription.js originally connects before registering. Check both bootstrap modes and later updates.

Bind permission to publish decoded values to the visit that received the frame. src/subscription.js permits Promise decoding and explicitly states that listener removal does not stop an existing decode. On close or replacement, retire that visit and check its permission immediately before publication. Check pending completion after close and switch while preserving active-visit delivery.

Establish retirement and cleanup ownership before startup can publish. src/workspace-navigation.js explicitly permits publication to synchronously switch or hide the panel. An older startup returning afterward must not overwrite the resulting visit's cleanup ownership. Check inline switch and hide, subsequent updates, and eventual cleanup.

Give each opening an independent lifetime even when it reuses the same transport. src/workspace-navigation.js explicitly supports transport reuse. Check that pending results from a retired opening remain suppressed while the later opening receives bootstrap and updates.

Scope the ordering repair to the presence subscription. The task forbids changing the metrics consumer, and src/metrics-consumer.js deliberately relies on attaching after synchronous bootstrap to count deltas only. Check that presence gains bootstrap delivery while metrics retain their existing output.

candidate_sources.docs/host-api.md: Store reads values and synchronously notifies saved integrations. Workspace exposes select(id), edit(text), close(), selection(), dispose(). Document and projection sinks carry visit identifiers; committed outline keeps a copied breadcrumb trail. Injected scheduler offers cancellable timer handles. Search preview is an adjacent transient consumer.

observations.summary: Close checkpoint: preserve the persistent document buffer independently of the departing view badge.
Preview-delay checkpoint: preserve the adjacent transient preview quiet interval.
Preview-hide checkpoint: hiding a preview discards its pending transient work.
Preview-reuse checkpoint: later preview input remains usable.
Quiet-burst checkpoint: coalesce edits and preserve the latest text after the declared quiet interval.
Save/close checkpoint: preserve synchronous close performed by a save callback.
Reopen checkpoint: document storage persists independently of a new opening of the same document.
Subsequent-burst checkpoint: later editing bursts must continue to save.
Switch checkpoint: preserve persistent document buffers and the lifetime of the current view badge.

unknowns: Dispose checkpoint: preserve the document-buffer persistence and view-cleanup behavior in public source.
Empty-edit checkpoint: preserve valid empty document text.
Save/navigation checkpoint: synchronous save callbacks may navigate; preserve the navigation chosen by that callback.
Public examples are not exhaustive; gold is independent.
